headlines.title: 한국판 IRA 내년 도입 …반도체·2차전지 등 생산 세액공제
headlines.summary: 한국판 인플레이션 감축법(IRA)이라 불리는 국내생산세액공제가 내년 도입된다. 3일 정부가 발표한 ‘2026년 세제개편안’에 담긴 내용이다. 반도체와 2차전지, 태양광발전, 풍력발전, 핵심 소재, 인공지능(AI) 로봇 부품 등 6대 분야에 한해 향후 10년간 소득세·법인세 공제 등 세제 혜택을 준다. 핵심 제조업 기반을 국내에 유지하기 위한 조치다.

top5_headlines.summary: 경제성장률 깜짝 성장에 근원물가도 올라 부동산 시장 여전히 불안…연속인상 무게 환율은 하향안정…주식시장 악화도 변수 소비자물가 상승률이 석 달 만에 2%대로 떨어졌지만 물가의 기조적 흐름을 보여주는 근원물가 상승률은 2년 7개월 만에 최고치를 기록했다.

top5_headlines.summary: 국가데이터처, 7월 소비자물가동향 발표 소비자물가상승률 5~6월 3%대에서 7월 2%대 회복 석유류 6월 24.7%→ 7월 15.5%…국제유가 하락 영향 '칩플레이션'으로 컴퓨터(25.1%) 등 전자기기 가격 ↑ 먹거리 물가 안정세…달걀·고등어 등 일부 품목 불안 생활물가상승률 2.

top5_headlines.title: AI · 반도체 국내생산 세액공제 … SMR도 최대 50% [2026 세제개편안]
top5_headlines.summary: 로봇·이차전지 등 6대분야 신설 지방 생산 기업일수록 우대 적용 정부가 인공지능(AI)·로봇과 반도체, 이차전지 등 경제안보 핵심 품목을 국내에서 직접 생산해 판매하는 기업에 세금을 깎아주는 ‘국내생산세액공제’를 신설한다. 소형모듈원전(SMR)과 초소형모듈원전(MMR)도 국가전략기술에 새로 포함해 연구개발(R&D) 비용의 최대 50%를 세액공제한다.

key_headlines.title: Record Tax Revenue Expected to Exceed 500 Trillion Won
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's first-half tax revenue reached 223 trillion won, up 33 trillion from the previous year. With semiconductor company tax prepayments expected in the second half, annual tax revenue could approach 450 trillion won with potential to surpass 500 trillion won next year.

key_headlines.title: Core Inflation Hits 31-Month High Despite Consumer Prices Cooling
key_headlines.summary: July consumer price inflation fell to 2.8% year-over-year, down from 3% levels, but core inflation reached a 31-month high of 2.6%, supporting expectations for continued rate hikes by the central bank.

key_headlines.title: Government Introduces Tax Credits for Domestic AI, Semiconductor Production
key_headlines.summary: The government announced new tax deduction schemes for domestic production of AI, semiconductors, and secondary batteries, with Small Modular Reactors eligible for up to 50% R&D tax credits as part of national strategy technology initiatives.

key_headlines.title: Second Quarter GDP Surprises with 0.6% Growth Despite High Base Effect
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's real GDP grew 0.6% quarter-over-quarter and 3.7% year-over-year in Q2, exceeding Bank of Korea's 0.2% forecast, driven by improved terms of trade from semiconductor export price increases.

key_headlines.title: Volatility Expected to Continue in Stock Markets Amid Interest Rate Uncertainty
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI experienced sharp fluctuations despite Samsung Electronics beating profit expectations, as investors weigh potential rate hikes against concerns about US long-term interest rates and geopolitical risks.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea is experiencing a semiconductor boom driving unprecedented tax revenue, with first-half collections reaching 223 trillion won and potential for the nation's first 500 trillion won annual tax revenue. However, this economic strength is creating inflationary pressures, as evidenced by core inflation hitting a 31-month high despite headline consumer prices cooling to 2.8%. The government is responding with tax incentives for strategic industries including AI, semiconductors, and secondary batteries, with small modular reactors receiving up to 50% R&D tax credits. These mixed signals are creating uncertainty about the central bank's monetary policy trajectory, with markets closely watching whether rate hikes will continue. The economic backdrop shows strong growth but mounting price pressures that are complicating policy decisions.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The second quarter delivered a growth surprise with 0.6% quarter-over-quarter GDP expansion, exceeding the Bank of Korea's 0.2% forecast and marking sustained momentum after Q1's 1.8% growth. Core inflation's rise to 2.6%, the highest in 31 months, strengthens the case for continued interest rate hikes despite headline inflation moderating to 2.8%. Real domestic income improved significantly, with real GDI growing 3.6% quarterly and 15.6% annually due to improved terms of trade from semiconductor export prices. Government monetary policy faces a complex calculus balancing below-target headline inflation against rising core inflation and growth momentum. Tax policy is shifting toward strategic industry support, with new production tax credits for AI, semiconductors, batteries, and nuclear technologies.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI experienced significant volatility, with Samsung Electronics reporting strong earnings that failed to prevent share price declines and broader market weakness. Savings bank deposit rates have declined from 4.5% to lower levels as investors redeployed funds from bonds to stocks, indicating shifting asset allocation preferences. Market direction appears heavily dependent on US long-term interest rates, with 10-year Treasury yields reaching post-2007 crisis highs following the Fed's July pause. Semiconductor and AI sector performance is particularly sensitive to US Treasury market dynamics, as rising long-term rates could dampen valuations for growth-oriented technology stocks. Professionals warn that elevated volatility will likely persist as markets digest interest rate expectations and geopolitical risks.
sections.Industry & Technology: The semiconductor industry remains the growth engine, with major chipmakers benefiting from AI-driven demand and driving overall economic performance. The government's new tax credit scheme for AI, semiconductors, secondary batteries, robots, and other strategic sectors aims to support domestic production with enhanced incentives for regional manufacturers. Secondary battery industry welcomed inclusion in tax incentive programs but expressed concern about limited scope, noting the absence of electric vehicle manufacturers from the value chain benefits. Espolytech, an engineering plastics specialist, achieved operating profit turnaround in the first half with US exports surging 78.9%, driven by AI data center and aerospace materials demand. Government Manufacturing AI Transform (M.AX) initiative shows promising results, with participating facilities achieving 30% productivity improvements and 15% reduction in defect rates.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment price increases moderated for the second consecutive week, with secondary-tier regions like Joong-rang and Nowon districts gaining relative strength as prices in Gangnam's premium areas cool. Government tax policy overhaul has created complexity, with different deduction thresholds and tax treatment depending on owner residency status, household property count, and regional location. Comprehensive property tax deductions will differentiate between resident single-property owners receiving 14 billion won and non-resident single-property owners receiving 9 billion won exemptions. Capital gains tax treatment has also become complicated, with real residency requirements and multiple variable factors making tax burden calculations difficult for property owners. The multi-tiered tax structure aims to promote housing accessibility but has generated confusion regarding actual tax obligations across different property ownership scenarios.
sections.International Economy: US equity markets achieved record highs in the Dow Jones while NASDAQ rallied 2% on falling oil prices, with the CME FedWatch reflecting 66.5% probability of at least 25 basis points rate increase in September FOMC meeting. Twenty-five US states have filed lawsuits against Trump tariffs, with enforcement actions continuing despite legal challenges, while companies across sectors report supply chain disruptions and cost pressures. The Trump administration is pursuing multipronged trade strategies including blacklisting Chinese open-source AI firms and considering restrictions on US cloud provider dealings with these companies. Japan has shifted policy toward defending the yen and avoiding national debt sales while facing US pressure to expand Federal Reserve bilateral currency swap arrangements (FIMA). China maintained firm negotiating positions on trade disputes during Trump's previous administration, suggesting potential for protracted negotiations ahead.
sections.AI & Economy: The US government is navigating tensions between AI regulation and free competition, with debates between enforcement-minded officials and Silicon Valley experts regarding Chinese open-source AI company restrictions. South Korea's manufacturing AI transformation initiative has demonstrated significant productivity gains of 30% and defect reductions of 15%, showcasing practical AI deployment benefits in industrial settings. Retail and distribution companies are expanding AI applications beyond chatbots into product planning, counterfeit detection, and sustainability monitoring, with capabilities for synthetic consumer research using AI-generated personas. Large US technology companies are investing heavily in AI infrastructure, but faces mounting concerns about unsustainable spending, with one analysis suggesting the five largest firms collectively face negative 178 trillion won in excess cash flow next year. AI infrastructure costs including electricity and equipment price inflation are creating macroeconomic headwinds, while market concerns about AI bubble risks are increasing despite acknowledged contributions to economic growth.
sections.Others: Denmark is significantly expanding military conscription in response to Russian security threats and Trump's pressure regarding Greenland integration, with even royal family members subject to mandatory service requirements. The US energy storage system market is emerging as critical grid infrastructure, creating new opportunities for Korean companies, particularly as tariffs on Chinese ESS lithium-ion batteries increase from 7.5% to 25% effective January 2026. South Korea is positioning its ESS component suppliers, including bus bar manufacturers and battery module assembly firms, to capture market share in American grid modernization projects. SpaceX reported 92% revenue growth in its first earnings release post-restructuring, with founder Elon Musk projecting 1 trillion dollar revenues by 2030 across aerospace and AI businesses. Hyundai Motor Group's 9 trillion won Saemangeum investment received support through expansion of national industrial complex to 426 hectares, enabling early development of AI data centers and robot factories.
